summary: Host key checking is on by default to block spoofing and MITM, but causes errors after reinstalls and prompts for new hosts. Disable with host_key_checking = False in ansible.cfg or ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING=False; it's slow in paramiko mode.
questions: How do I stop Ansible prompting to accept host keys?
How do I disable host key checking in Ansible?
Why does Ansible fail after I reinstalled a server?
Is it safe to turn off host key checking?

answer_card.title: Disable host key checking
answer_card.answer_md:
Host key checking protects against spoofing and man-in-the-middle attacks. It errors when a reinstalled host has a new key, and prompts for unknown hosts (bad for cron).

If you accept the risk:
```ini
# /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg or ~/.ansible.cfg
[defaults]
host_key_checking = False
```
or `export ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING=False`. In paramiko mode host key checking is slow, so prefer `ssh`.
